review_candidates.title: Talent strategist
review_candidates.description: At Bending Spoons, we’re striving to build one of the all-time great companies. A company that serves a huge number of customers. A company where team members grow to their full potential. A company that functions at unparalleled levels of effectiveness and efficiency. A company that creates value for shareowners at an extraordinary rate. And a company that does so while adhering to high ethical standards. In pursuit of this objective, we acquire and improve digital businesses, not to sell on, but to own and operate for the long term. The transformations we make are often deep—designed to speed up innovation, benefit customers, and strengthen business performance. Here, hierarchy is minimal and teams are small and talent-dense. We operate established products with the ambition, agility, and urgency of a startup. Across the company, we integrate AI deeply into how we work so that human judgment and machine intelligence reinforce each other. For a talented, driven, and collaborative individual, working at Bending Spoons is an opportunity to learn, make an impact, and progress their career at an exceptionally high rate. That’s our promise to such a candidate. A few examples of your responsibilities Shape our talent strategy. Define and improve how we hire, navigate the trade-offs that determine where effort and investment create the most value, and ensure that hiring remains a competitive advantage for Bending Spoons. Continuously experiment and improve. Challenge assumptions, run rigorous experiments, and use evidence to identify better ways to attract, assess, and hire outstanding people. Own hiring end-to-end. Run the full recruiting loop—from sourcing to final decision—using AI and modern tooling to accelerate the process while applying human judgment where it matters most. Find exceptional talent. Proactively identify and engage top candidates across multiple channels, combining outreach, data, and new technologies to surface the strongest people. Build high-signal evaluations. Design and run structured assessments—tests, interviews, and other evaluation methods—that produce clear signal and support confident hiring decisions. What we look for Reasoning ability. Given the necessary knowledge, you can solve complex problems. You think from first principles, and structure your ideas sharply. You resist the influence of biases. You identify and take care of the details that matter. Drive. You’re extremely ambitious in everything you do—and your initiative, effort, and tenacity match the intensity of your ambition. You feel deeply responsible for your work. You hold yourself to a high—and rising—bar. Team spirit. You give generously and without the expectation of receiving in return. You support the best idea, not your idea. You're always happy to get your hands dirty to help your team. You’re reliable, honest, and transparent. Proficiency in English. You read, write, and speak proficiently in English. What we offer Incredibly talented, entrepreneurial teams. You’ll work in small, result-oriented, autonomous teams alongside some of the brightest people in your field. An exceptional opportunity for growth. We go to great lengths to hire individuals of outstanding potential—then, our priority is to put them in the ideal position to thrive. Spooners in their 20s lead products worth hundreds of millions of dollars. And if you’ve got what it takes, you’ll soon be playing an essential role in major projects, too. All. These. Benefits. Flexible hours, remote working, unlimited backing for learning and training, top-of-the-market health insurance, a rich relocation package, generous parental support, and a yearly retreat to a stunning location. We help each Spooner set up the conditions to do their best work. Competitive pay and access to company equity at a discount. Typical annual salary offers range from £56,345 to £85,797 in London and from €54,346 to €82,557 elsewhere in Europe. The lower end of these ranges applies to candidates with little or no relevant experience, while exceptionally experienced candidates may receive offers of up to £196,764 in London or €188,848 elsewhere in Europe. Candidates offered a permanent contract may choose to receive part of their compensation in discounted company equity. Commitment & contract Permanent or fixed-term. Full-time or part-time. Location Milan (Italy), London (UK), Madrid (Spain), Warsaw (Poland), or fully remote from eligible countries. The selection process In our screening process, we prioritize verifiable signals of excellence, regardless of seniority. There are no preferential paths beyond what your application demonstrates, and we evaluate every candidate through the same process. Some people hold back because they feel they lack experience or have an “imperfect” CV. If you like the role and believe you could excel over time, don’t self-reject. All applications go through our careers page, which is the only way to be considered. If you pass our screening, you’ll be asked to complete one or more tests. They are challenging, may involve unfamiliar problems, and can take several hours. To learn more about what to expect throughout the selection process, you can find additional information here. We set the bar high and won’t extend an offer until we’re confident we’ve found the right candidate. This is why a job may remain open for months or be reposted several times. We consider all applicants for employment and provide reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities—please let us know through this form. Before you apply If you’ve applied before but didn't receive an offer, we recommend waiting at least one year before applying again. Bending Spoons is a demanding environment. We’re extremely ambitious and we hold ourselves—and one another—to a high standard. While this tends to lead to extraordinary learning, achievement, and career growth, it also requires significant commitment. To help you ramp up quickly and set yourself up for success, we expect you to spend most days in our Milan office during your first few months with us, regardless of your long-term work location. It’s the best way to rapidly absorb our company culture and build trust with your new teammates. We’ll support you with generous travel and accommodation assistance. After that, you’re welcome to work from one of our offices, or remotely from approved countries—depending on what we agree at the offer stage. If the role speaks to you and you’re excited to give your best, we’d love to hear from you. Apply now—we can’t wait to meet you.

review_candidates.title: Strategic Financial Analyst (Seattle, Washington)
review_candidates.description: This role requires candidates to be currently located in the Seattle area and able to work onsite 2 days per week. This is not a remote position. Our Company Beale Infrastructure partners with the world's leading technology companies to develop data centers and infrastructure in regions with strong access to carbon-free energy. Our team of industry veterans brings together deep experience executing data center, real estate, infrastructure and renewable energy projects. We understand the complexities of hyperscale data center development, construction and operations and we are committed to delivering world class projects to our customers through strong partnerships. We offer fully capitalized site acquisition, development and build-to-suit data center construction solutions. We partner closely with power utilities on generation and infrastructure strategies, and our investments create high-quality jobs and generate substantial new tax revenues for communities. Carbon-free energy resources drive Beale's site selection and growth strategies. Environmental stewardship is at the forefront of Beale's site selection and investment strategies, and we partner closely with communities to understand local resource constraints and develop responsible roadmaps for growth. We strive to be the employer of choice and to foster strong partnerships with vendors and communities. To learn more, visit www.bealeinfra.com. We are a high-growth portfolio company backed by Blue Owl – www.blueowl.com. The Role As we continue to grow, we are seeking team members who thrive in dynamic environments, enjoy solving complex problems, and are excited by the opportunity to help build processes and capabilities from the ground up. This is not a traditional analyst role. This role offers a unique opportunity for an early-career finance professional to develop a broad finance skill set and to gain exposure across FP&A, Accounting, Treasury, Capital Markets and other disciplines. The FP&A Analyst will support a wide range of financial planning and analysis activities while helping establish the processes, tools, and reporting frameworks needed to support a rapidly evolving organization. Key Responsibilities Financial Analysis Develop and maintain financial models to support business planning, investment decisions, and deal financing. Identify and analyze key drivers to key financial metrics. Prepare recurring management reporting packages, dashboards, and KPI analyses. Assist with board, lender, tenant, and investor reporting requirements. Cross-Functional Finance Exposure Support treasury activities including cash forecasting and liquidity planning. Assist with capital markets, financing, and lender-related analyses and reporting. Support full project financing lifecycle from due diligence to project completion. Collaborate with broader finance and operational teams to refine project budgets, understand business drivers, and performance metrics. Strategic & Ad Hoc Analysis Perform financial and operational analyses to support strategic initiatives and business decisions. Analyze trends in revenue, costs, profitability, liquidity, and operational performance. Identify opportunities to improve reporting, forecasting accuracy, and financial insights. Support special projects and cross-functional initiatives as business needs evolve. Process Development & Ownership Lead projects to create and improve FP&A processes, reporting tools, and analytical frameworks. Help establish scalable financial processes appropriate for a growing organization. Drive continuous improvement initiatives and recommend more efficient ways of working. Document processes and support finance system enhancements, as needed. Qualifications Required Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business, or a related field. 2 years of experience in finance (FP&A, treasury, capital markets), investment banking, consulting, or a related analytical role. Strong analytical, quantitative, and problem-solving skills. Advanced proficiency in Excel and financial modeling. High level of intellectual curiosity and willingness to learn. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Self-starter mindset with the ability to work independently and take ownership of projects, as well as to collaborate with others across disciplines Preferred Experience working with financial reporting systems, BI tools, and ERP platforms. Experience leveraging AI tools Exposure to forecasting, budgeting, or financial statement analysis. Understanding of accounting principles and corporate finance concepts. Familiarity with infrastructure, industrials, construction, energy, utilities, or related sectors. Familiarity with interpreting, assessing and informing contract/legal documents What Will Make You Successful You are energized by building something rather than simply maintaining existing processes. You are comfortable operating without perfect information and can create structure where little exists. You are intellectually curious, comfortable in navigating ambiguity, and eager to contribute beyond a defined job description. You proactively seek opportunities to improve the business and ask questions that challenge assumptions. You enjoy moving between detailed analysis and big-picture thinking. You are eager to gain exposure across multiple finance disciplines and among cross functional teams. You thrive in a high-accountability, entrepreneurial environment where priorities can evolve quickly. It is expected that the base annual salary range for this position will be $85,000 - $110,000. Pursuant to any applicable law or regulation, the anticipated salary range may include a performance-based discretionary annual bonus. Factors that may affect a candidate's starting pay within this range include geography, skills, experience and other qualifications for the role. This full-time position is eligible for generous benefits, including health, dental, and 401 (k). Beale Infrastructure Group is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We evaluate qualified applicants without regard to race, color, national origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, protected veteran status, and other statuses protected by law.

The Site Construction Manager will act as a key interface between the Client, EPC Contractor, WSP project team and discipline specialists to ensure that construction activities are executed safely, in accordance with the EPC Contract, approved drawings, specifications, quality requirements and project schedule. The role will drive EPC performance, monitor site progress, coordinate issue resolution, follow up on pending actions, support construction readiness and ensure timely escalation of risks, delays and non-compliances Responsibilities Lead site construction supervision and coordination for EPC works, ensuring that construction activities are executed in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, EPC Contract requirements, project procedures and applicable codes and standards. Act as the day-to-day site interface with the Client, EPC Contractor and WSP project team for construction-related matters, including progress, priorities, constraints, site issues and action closure. Drive EPC Contractor performance by monitoring daily site activities, manpower, equipment deployment, material availability, work fronts and adherence to the approved construction schedule. Coordinate with the Client and EPC Contractor to ensure that the WSP scope of works is completed smoothly, with timely technical inputs, site responses, inspections, reporting and issue escalation. Monitor construction interfaces between civil, mechanical, electrical, I&C, commissioning and HSE teams, and drive closure of interface issues that may affect schedule, quality or safety. Review construction method statements, ITPs, work permits, risk assessments, lifting plans, temporary works and construction procedures, and coordinate comments with relevant discipline specialists. Participate in site progress meetings, construction coordination meetings, Client meetings, EPC meetings and project review meetings, and ensure that key actions are recorded, assigned and followed up to closure. Prepare and circulate minutes of meetings, action trackers, site observation reports and construction follow-up notes for meetings and site inspections attended. Coordinate with discipline engineers for resolution of RFIs/TQs, design clarifications, field changes, site instructions, inspection comments and technical constraints raised during construction. Support construction planning, sequencing and readiness reviews, including review of look-ahead schedules, critical path activities, work front availability and construction constraints. Monitor site quality and HSE compliance in coordination with dedicated QA/QC and HSE teams, and ensure that construction observations, NCRs, punch items and corrective actions are properly tracked and closed. Coordinate site communications with the Client and EPC Contractor, and support timely escalation of risks, delays, manpower shortfalls, material constraints and unresolved technical or contractual matters. Support mechanical completion, pre-commissioning, commissioning readiness, punch list closure and handover activities by ensuring construction completion status is properly verified and documented. Maintain construction action logs, issue registers, RFI/TQ trackers, site instruction logs, NCR/punch list trackers and other follow-up tools required to drive timely closure. Provide inputs to construction progress reports, including physical progress, critical activities, constraints, delay events, recovery measures, manpower trends and key decisions required. Support review of EPC Contractor invoices, progress claims and milestone submissions by confirming construction progress, site records and supporting evidence as required. Ensure construction documentation and handover records are complete, traceable and aligned with project requirements, including redlines, as-built inputs, completion dossiers and final closeout records. Qualifications Must have minimum Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Electrical Engineering discipline from an internationally recognized University. Minimum 15 years’ relevant experience, including substantial site construction management experience on CCGT, cogeneration, thermal power or large industrial EPC projects, with at least 5 years in a Construction Manager/Site Construction Manager or equivalent leadership role. Professional registration/certification is preferred. Strong capability in site reporting, construction documentation, progress tracking, action management, MS Office, document control systems and relevant project controls tools is required. Experience in construction supervision of CCGT/cogeneration projects involving GT, ST, HRSG, generators, BOP systems, substations, cooling systems and major civil/structural works. Experience supporting mechanical completion, pre-commissioning, commissioning readiness, punch list closeout and handover dossier preparation. Prior experience in KSA or GCC power project sites and familiarity with regional Client, EPC Contractor and permitting requirements is an advantage.
